name: api-core-plate-controller-docs
title: Plate Controller
description: Connect shared React UI to the active Plate editor.

files.content:
--- title: Plate Controller description: Connect shared React UI to the active Plate editor. --- `PlateController` lets shared toolbars, panels, and inspectors resolve an editor outside a single `Plate` subtree. ## Usage Wrap the shared UI and participating editors in `PlateController`. `PlateContent` automatically registers each editor for its mounted lifetime. ```tsx title="components/editor-shell.tsx" import { Plate, PlateContent, PlateController, useCreateEditor, useOptionalEditor, } from 'platejs/react'; export function EditorShell() { const main = useCreateEditor({ id: 'main' }); const secondary = useCreateEditor({ id: 'secondary' }); return ( ); } function ActiveEditorLabel() { const editor = useOptionalEditor(); return

{editor ? `Active editor: ${editor.id}` : 'No editor selected.'}

; } ``` Set `primary` on `Plate`; it defaults to `true`. A view with `primary={false}` can become active when focused. IDs are application labels; one model and ID can have several mounted views. ## Editor lookup `useEditor()` returns the nearest provider’s selected editor and throws when no target exists. `useOptionalEditor()` uses the same selection and returns `null` without a provider or target. - Inside `PlateContent`, hooks use that exact editable view, including its root, DOM, and current read-only state. - Inside `Plate`, outside its content, UI follows that Plate’s last focused view, then its first mounted view. A Plate without content provides its model. - Shared UI under the controller uses the last focused mounted view, then the first mounted primary view before focus or after target removal. - Nested `Plate` and `PlateController` components scope their descendants independently. Blur retains the active view for toolbar interaction. `PlateContent` owns registration and cleanup; only views with editable DOM participate in controller selection. ## Captured interactions Use `EditorProvider` to bind controls to an existing editor. For example, a popup can capture the value returned by `useEditor()` when it opens and keep that target until it closes. ```tsx import { EditorProvider } from 'platejs/react'; ``` `EditorProvider` accepts `editor: Editor | null` and `children: React.ReactNode`; it creates no editable view. React portals retain this context. Commands read the target’s current permissions. Read-only or unmounted targets reject writes, and captured interactions never select a replacement view automatically. ## API Reference `PlateController` accepts only `children: React.ReactNode`. The `primary` prop on `Plate` controls initial and fallback eligibility. For state and focus subscriptions, see [Editor Context](/docs/plate/api/core/plate-store).
